name: Contrastive identity learning with hard/ambiguous neighbour pairs on top of ready features (QDTrack CVPR 2021; MASA CVPR 2024 training recipe; UCSL ICCV 2023 ambiguity contrast; FocalLink 2026; adapters for ReID)
bibliography: (1) QDTrack: Jiangmiao Pang, Linlu Qiu, Xia Li, Haofeng Chen, Qi Li, Trevor Darrell, Fisher Yu. 'Quasi-Dense Similarity Learning for Multiple Object Tracking'. CVPR 2021 (oral); arXiv:2006.06664 v4 (8 Sep 2021), https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.06664 (read via ar5iv https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2006.06664). Code: https://github.com/SysCV/qdtrack (config opened). A TPAMI extension (QDTrack journal version) exists [uncertain: not opened, not an independent confirmation]. (2) MASA: Siyuan Li, Lei Ke, Martin Danelljan, Luigi Piccinelli, Mattia Segu, Luc Van Gool, Fisher Yu. 'Matching Anything by Segmenting Anything'. CVPR 2024 (Highlight); arXiv:2406.04221, https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04221 ; CVF https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/papers/Li_Matching_Anything_by_Segmenting_Anything_CVPR_2024_paper.pdf ; code https://github.com/siyuanliii/masa (loss, track head, train config, BDD tracker opened); weights https://huggingface.co/dereksiyuanli/masa. (4) FocalLink: Yanting Zhang, Wujian Huang, Cairong Yan, Rui Fan, Gaoang Wang, Jenq-Neng Hwang. 'FocalLink: Densely Modulated Contrastive Learning for Trajectory Association in Multi-Object Tracking'. (5) Adapters / hard-negative mining for ReID: no single adapter-for-ReID paper with a frozen-base + hard-pair ablation was found in a short search (candidates seen only as search snippets: MoDA 2025, DM-Adapter arXiv 2503.04144, AdalReID arXiv 2405.19005, SANER CVPR 2026); the canonical batch-hard mining reference is Hermans, Beyer, Leibe, 'In Defense of the Triplet Loss for Person Re-Identification', arXiv:1703.07737 (2017) [uncertain: cited from prior knowledge, not opened]. Residual-alpha adapters over a frozen base (Tip-Adapter, CLIP-Adapter, zero-init) are covered by item C01 and not repeated here.

inputs_state_output: QDTrack: single appearance branch (ResNet-50 FPN Faster R-CNN; embedding head 4 conv + 1 FC, 256-d, RoIAlign 7x7) trained on a key frame and a reference frame from its +/-3 frame neighbourhood; state = per-track embedding memory with momentum update and one-frame backdrops (unmatched detections kept as negative candidates); output = bi-directional softmax similarity, mutual nearest-neighbour matching. No weak/added branch: Table 5 adds IoU, motion and box-regression cues to the appearance score as a post-hoc ablation. MASA: frozen foundation backbone (SAM / Detic / Grounding-DINO / R50 detector) + trained MASA adapter (multi-scale features, deformable dynamic fusion, RoIAlign, QDTrack-style embedding head 256-d); training pairs come from two strong augmentations of ONE still image with SAM masks as region proposals; inference memory: 10 tracklet frames, momentum 0.8, bi-softmax, no motion model in the BDD tracker. UCSL: FairMOT DLA-34 joint detector+ReID trained without identity labels by self-, cross- and ambiguity-contrast between frames; association = embedding distance then IoU with a Kalman filter. FocalLink: post-hoc trajectory-segment encoder: per detection a 2048-d ReID embedding + 4-d box -> 512-d projection -> 4 dense focal-modulation blocks over time -> binary 'same entity' classifier for two tracklet segments; plugged on top of existing trackers (FLWN, FeatureSORT, FairMOT, PermaTrack, TrackFormer, TransCenter). Ours: frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign 256-d embedding of every real detection region compared with the snapped exemplar, the tagged previous target and an EMA bank (alpha 0.5), plus relative versions, geometry and tagged geometry, fed to gradient boosting; FlyVis branch = 238 per-region features (68 regional activity features of 34 output types incl. T4/T5 and neighbour means, plus relative transforms) from a bounded grey crop with recurrent state over exemplar+search frames; two-stage readout identity -> full-box transfer gate. Key difference: in all four sources the trained branch IS the appearance branch (or a temporal encoder of appearance); none trains a second, weaker modality only on pairs that a frozen appearance base confuses.
fusion_and_training: QDTrack: no fusion; the embedding head is trained jointly with the detector (loss L = L_det + 0.25 L_embed + 1.0 L_aux); motion/IoU cues in Table 5 are combined 'following Tracktor' without a stated formula and barely change or slightly lower the result. MASA: backbone frozen (freeze_detector=True in the train config), only the adapter + embedding head trained, SGD lr 0.08; an auxiliary detection head (object-prior distillation) is trained and dropped at inference; nothing prevents degrading the base because the base is frozen and the adapter output replaces (not adds to) the base features for matching. UCSL: everything trained jointly from a COCO/CrowdHuman detector initialisation, no frozen base. FocalLink: two-stage training - Stage 1: 200 epochs contrastive pre-training of the encoder with the classifier frozen; Stage 2: 300 epochs joint training of the full network with the contrastive weight gradually reduced (AdamW lr 3e-4, batch 32); the base tracker is untouched and FocalLink only re-links its tracklets; the element-wise modulation Y = gamma*X + beta*C (Eq. 3) keeps a learnable identity path from input features, an implicit residual. None of the sources uses zero-init, residual alpha on a second modality, cue masking or training restricted to base-confused pairs; none has a mechanism against the added branch being ignored, because there is no separate weak branch. Transfer: for 'train only the FlyVis addition on MASA-confused pairs' the protective mechanisms must come from elsewhere (C01 residual alpha=0 start, C02 unimodal pre-training): freeze MASA and the existing base model, train a small FlyVis-only scorer on confused episodes, add it as a residual logit with weight alpha chosen on calibration videos and alpha=0 as the built-in fallback.
labels_and_loss: QDTrack: RoIs from the RPN assigned positive if IoU > 0.7 with a ground-truth box and negative if IoU < 0.3 (MaxIoUAssigner, min_pos_iou 0.5); 128 key RoIs vs 256 reference RoIs, positive:negative 1:1 in the paper; the official config uses CombinedSampler num=256, pos_fraction 0.5, InstanceBalancedPosSampler for positives and RandomSampler for negatives (the paper text mentions IoU-balanced sampling - a paper/code discrepancy). Negatives therefore include other objects AND background RoIs of the reference frame, i.e. all neighbours are negatives, with no explicit similarity-based hard mining in the main loss. Main loss: multi-positive cross-entropy L_embed = log[1 + sum_{k+} sum_{k-} exp(v.k- - v.k+)] (Eq. 5); auxiliary L2 on cosine (cos - c)^2 with all positives and 3x negatives (Eq. 6), implemented as L2Loss with hard_mining=True, neg_pos_ub=3, neg_margin 0.1 - the only explicit hard-negative mining, and it is on the auxiliary term. MASA: positives = the same SAM instance under two augmentations of one image; negatives = other SAM instances ('different instances'; exact pool not stated in text); loss = UnbiasedContrastLoss (multi-positive cross-entropy with positive normalisation, code unbiased_contrastive_loss.py) weight 0.25 + MarginL2Loss aux with hard_mining=True, neg_pos_ub=3, neg_margin 0.1, weight 1.0; CombinedSampler num=512, pos_fraction 0.5; temperature 0.07 stated in the paper. Up to 256 proposals per batch (Table 9b) - more same-image instances = more near negatives. UCSL: no identity labels; ambiguity contrast = objects whose cross-frame similarity is below theta=0.7 are 'ambiguous', their re-matching distributions S_r are made confident by a minimum-entropy loss weighted by 1/(|N_r - M_r| + 1); no explicit push/pull of specific pairs and no pseudo-labels. FocalLink: binary cross-entropy for 'same entity' + supervised contrastive loss (SupCon form, Eq. 8) over L2-normalised embeddings, positives = segments of the same identity in the batch, all others negatives, temperature tau (value not given); no hard-negative mining described. Class imbalance: handled in QDTrack/MASA by fixed positive fraction and neg_pos_ub=3; not discussed in UCSL/FocalLink. None uses 'consequence of assignment' labels. Hermans et al. (not opened) [uncertain]: batch-hard triplet - for each anchor the farthest positive and nearest negative in a PK batch.
data_camera_resolution_rate: QDTrack: BDD100K tracking 1,400 train videos (278k images), 200 val videos, 30 fps video annotated at 5 fps, 8 classes, inference at 1296x720, moving dash camera, day/night/weather mix (no per-condition breakdown reported); also MOT17 (longer side 1088), Waymo, TAO. MASA: training on unlabeled still images (SA-1B subset for SAM-based models [uncertain: exact subset size not re-checked]); zero-shot evaluation on BDD100K MOT val (same 200 videos, 5 fps annotation), BDD MOTS, TAO, YouTube-VIS. UCSL: MOT15/MOT17/MOT20 pedestrians, static and moving cameras, pre-training COCO + CrowdHuman; no BDD100K. FocalLink: MOT17 and MOT20 (pedestrians, crowded MOT20), split for evaluation not stated (probably test-server numbers [uncertain]); no BDD100K, no low light. Ours: BDD100K MOT val-derived 130 videos (fit84 + fit20 + train26) at the bench frame rate, low light/glare/occlusion/clutter subsets.

distinguishing_ablations: QDTrack Table 5 is the only source here that isolates a weak motion cue over a strong appearance base, and it is on BDD100K: adding IoU, motion or box regression to quasi-dense appearance gives -0.3 to -0.2 mMOTA and -1.0 to -0.7 mIDF1 (negative or null), while the same cues alone are 8-10 mMOTA points below appearance - a direct published analogue of our hybrid result (appearance strong, weak cue adds nothing). Its Table 4 isolates the sampling: dense (all RoIs, including neighbours and background) vs sparse sampling +4.8 IDF1, multi-positive +1.0 IDF1 - the gain is from MORE and NEARBY negatives, not from a second branch. MASA Table 9b: more proposals (more same-image near negatives) 47.1 -> 51.9 AssocA on BDD; Table 8: training the adapter over frozen SAM features 32.9 -> 48.5 AssocA - adaptation of the SAME modality on hard same-image instance pairs over a frozen base. No equal-capacity non-informative control, no seeds. UCSL Table 4: the ambiguity-contrast module (the one aimed at confusable pairs) gives -0.2 IDF1, -0.1 HOTA, -387 IDs on MOT17 - essentially null on identity metrics; single run. FocalLink Table 2: contrastive term on/off inside the same added module, +0.08 to +1.25 HOTA on MOT20, but ATA drops for FairMOT; there is no row 'base tracker + equal-capacity module without ReID' or 'without box input', so the contribution of motion (box) vs appearance input is not isolated; single runs. Hermans et al. (not opened) [uncertain]: batch-hard vs batch-all comparisons exist but on a single modality. Net: no source shows a weaker second modality trained only on base-confused pairs giving a gain over a frozen strong appearance base; the one clean motion-over-appearance ablation (QDTrack Table 5, BDD100K) is negative.
explanations_addressed: (a) Fly features carry no unique identity beyond appearance: caution, direct analogue - QDTrack Table 5 on BDD100K shows box motion cues add nothing to strong learned appearance; our train26 +0.107 [-0.176; +0.400] pp is consistent with that. Not proof for FlyVis pixel motion, which differs from box motion. (b) Information exists but fusion ignores it: not addressed (no source has a separate weak branch); the hard-pair training proposed here is one remedy to test: if FlyVis carries information only on confused pairs, a scorer trained on all regions dilutes it by the ~88% of queries appearance already solves - restricting training and evaluation to confused episodes directly tests this. (c) Saved readout lost it, new activity or fine-tuned core needed: design analogy - MASA Table 8 shows a large gain from training an adapter over frozen generic features (32.9 -> 48.5 AssocA) using near-negative instance pairs; the analogue is training the FlyVis readout/core on confused pairs rather than relying on fixed saved features; but MASA's gain is in the same modality. (d) FlyVis lacks a lobula/identity pathway: not addressed. (e) Motion helps only in subsets diluted by averaging: partially - hard-pair mining is exactly a subset focus; our count shows the subset is small (exemplar top-1 wrong in 231 of 1,959 fit104 and 61 of 501 train26 multi-region queries), which caps any effect. (f) Ceiling too low: informs it - the perfect-identity ceiling (+2.84 [1.87; 3.83] pp on train26) is the gain of fixing ALL identity errors; a fly branch that only fixes a fraction of the confused episodes can reach at most that fraction of the gap between the current base (+0.66 pp) and the ceiling, so a +2 pp criterion is out of reach unless the fly branch fixes most base errors.
evidence_strength: QDTrack: peer-reviewed CVPR oral, widely replicated, code verified (sampler/loss config read); Table 5 is a single-run ablation without CI and the fusion formula for motion cues is not stated - moderate. MASA: peer-reviewed CVPR highlight, code verified (frozen detector, loss and sampler read); same group and same head as QDTrack, so not an independent confirmation; ablations single-run - moderate. UCSL: peer-reviewed ICCV, ablation single-run on one dataset, code not checked - weak for our question. FocalLink: peer-reviewed 4-page ICASSP, no code, no CI, tiny gains, a table inconsistency (ATA drops with CL for FairMOT) - weak. Adapter/ReID hard-mining: not verified in this short check - none. Overall for 'weak branch trained on base-confused pairs adds over frozen strong appearance': weak (no direct evidence); for 'motion cue adds nothing over strong appearance on BDD100K': moderate (QDTrack Table 5).
difference_from_tried: Different in training target, not in features: everything tried trained the identity gradient boosting on ALL real regions of all queries with MASA cosines and FlyVis features concatenated (base_D vs base); no model has been trained on (i) only episodes where the frozen appearance base is wrong or uncertain, or (ii) pairwise/contrastive targets between the target region and its nearest-in-appearance neighbour, or (iii) as a residual correction to a frozen base logit. The prepared core fine-tuning script (scripts/z13_core_identity_20261026.py) trains the 734 core parameters with cross-entropy over regions of the same class, again on all episodes of fit84, not restricted to MASA-confused ones and not as a residual over MASA. Not different: the features themselves (saved D/C/R1 238-d) and the boosting family; a boosting model on confused episodes alone is close to what nested folds already approximate, so the difference must come from the residual/frozen-base formulation and the evaluation on the confused subset.
math_precheck: All CPU, saved data only, no core training. Data already saved: per query the MASA 256-d embeddings of every real region and the exemplar (runs/z13_masa_regions_20261026/recovery1/videos/*.npz), truth identity per region slot (ident in runs/z13_identity_gate_tagged_20261026/features_{D,C,R1}.npz for fit104 and runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/train26_features_*.npz for train26), FlyVis features F1 (238-d per region) for D, C and R1, tagged geometry, previous-query links (temporal_readiness.json). Missing: out-of-fold per-region base scores (only AUC saved) - regenerate by re-running the base arm with the same nested folds. Step 1 (size of the target set): with out-of-fold base logits define confused episodes = queries with target present and a neighbour whose base score is within margin m of the target or above it, plus target-absent queries where the base accepts a neighbour; report counts per video (exemplar-only counts already: 231/1,959 fit104, 61/501 train26 top-1 wrong). Step 2 (complementarity on confused episodes): on those episodes only, train a FlyVis-only pairwise scorer (logistic regression or small boosting on difference of fly features target-vs-neighbour, video-grouped nested folds) and measure (a) pairwise accuracy of fly on base-wrong episodes vs 50%, (b) the same for R1 eye input and for no-fly geometry/velocity differences of equal dimension. Step 3 (residual oracle bound): base logit + alpha * fly residual with alpha selected on fit20 calibration only; compute the fraction of base-wrong episodes flipped to correct minus base-correct episodes flipped to wrong (net flips) and run it through the existing gate/utility code to get utility in pp with paired bootstrap over videos. Upper bound before any of this: utility gain <= (net flips / all base errors) x (ceiling - base) = f x (2.84 - 0.66) pp on train26; to reach the +2 pp pre-registered criterion f would need ~0.92 - effectively impossible; to clear a CI-positive +0.3 pp f must be >= ~0.14 [uncertain: assumes utility roughly linear in fixed errors]. Decision rule: STOP the GPU branch (no core fine-tuning on confused pairs) if on fit104 confused episodes (i) fly pairwise accuracy on base-wrong pairs has 95% CI including 50% or is not above R1/no-fly controls by a CI-positive margin, or (ii) net flips at the calibrated alpha are <= 0 or the implied utility bound is < +0.3 pp; only if both pass, run the single registered train26 check of the residual model, and only if that is CI-positive over base AND over base+R1 consider core fine-tuning with a confused-pair loss.
cue_role_and_regime: Role: training-time sample selector plus a residual identity score - the FlyVis cue enters as a small scorer trained only on hard pairs (target vs nearest-in-appearance neighbour, or base-accepted wrong region) and added to the frozen base logit with weight alpha; optionally as a pairwise contrastive loss for the readout or core. Regime: same class and similar look (MASA cosine margin small), crossing/adjacent neighbours, and target-absent queries where a neighbour is wrongly accepted; darkness/glare only insofar as they make MASA confuse regions (conditions should be reported per subset, but the confused pool is already small, ~61 train26 exemplar errors, so per-condition CI will be wide). In QDTrack/MASA the 'hard' pairs are same-frame/same-image neighbours and background, which matches our regime of neighbour regions inside one query.
no_fly_equivalent_control: Same residual scorer, same confused episodes, same capacity, same alpha selection, with inputs (1) eye input R1 features (already saved, 238-d), (2) stock FlyVis C (saved), (3) no-fly geometry/velocity differences (box centre displacement vs tagged previous target, size ratio, Kalman-predicted IoU, velocity direction consistency from saved geometry and Gtag) padded/projected to the same dimension, (4) a random-feature control of equal dimension (shuffled fly features within video) to measure overfitting on the small confused pool. Three-way comparison required by the project rule: base / base + residual(no-fly) / base + residual(fly D); FlyVis result only if (3) > (2) with CI-positive paired bootstrap, and modernisation only if D > C.
bio_node_mapping: No biological counterpart in the sources (contrastive training is an engineering objective). In FlyVis terms the change targets the readout node (a learned per-region discriminator over the 34 output types incl. T4/T5 and neighbour means), or, if run on GPU, the core parameters (734, connectome-constrained) trained with a target-vs-distractor objective - loosely analogous to lobula object cells (LC/LPLC) that respond to a selected object against distractors (FlyWire 783 connectome available in data/flywire/783), but no source supports that mapping.
novelty_overlap: Nearest prior: QDTrack/MASA dense same-frame negative contrastive learning of appearance and FocalLink's contrastive plug-in over tracklets; a connectome-constrained motion branch trained only on frozen-appearance-confused pairs is not described in them, but the novelty is modest and only meaningful if it beats the R1/no-fly residual of equal capacity.
candidate_node_change: Node: FlyVis readout (CPU version) then, conditionally, core parameters (GPU version). Version A (CPU, saved features): freeze MASA and the existing base gradient boosting; regenerate its out-of-fold logits; train a residual FlyVis scorer r(fly_target_region - fly_neighbour_region, fly_region) only on confused episodes (fit84 train, fit20 calibration for alpha and the margin m), combined as logit = base + alpha * r with alpha grid including 0; evaluate identity on confused episodes and utility through the existing transfer gate. It addresses the FlyVis problem that its saved activity adds no unique identity information over appearance when trained on all regions - if information exists only where appearance fails, this concentrates the training signal there. Version B (GPU, only if A passes): run scripts/z13_core_identity_20261026.py with episodes restricted to MASA-confused pairs and a QDTrack-style multi-positive loss with nearest-appearance neighbours as negatives, keeping the stock core as the init and the fit20 stop gate. Controls: appearance only (base), base + residual(R1), base + residual(C), base + residual(no-fly geometry/velocity of equal dimension), base + residual(shuffled). Condition to proceed to GPU: Version A fly residual CI-positive over base AND over the R1 and no-fly residuals on fit104 nested folds, net flips > 0, implied utility bound >= +0.3 pp; then a single registered train26 check.
strongest_objection: The only clean published ablation of a motion cue over strong learned appearance on BDD100K (QDTrack Table 5) is negative, and none of the sources trains a second modality only on base-confused pairs - the mechanism is an extrapolation. The confused pool is tiny (exemplar top-1 wrong in 231 fit104 and 61 train26 queries; fewer for the full base), so a scorer trained on it is likely to overfit and its effect on per-video utility cannot be resolved by a 26-video bootstrap; even fixing every confused episode yields at most the ceiling minus the base (about +2.2 pp on train26), and realistic fractions give a few tenths of a pp. The existing hybrid already gave the fly features access to these episodes through boosting, which can learn interaction splits on MASA margin, so restricting training may change little.
cost_and_hardware: Version A and the whole precheck: CPU only, saved features; regenerating out-of-fold base logits and fitting residual scorers with nested folds and bootstrap is about the cost of one hybrid run (the v2 internal run took ~2,275 s per runs/z13_hybrid_identity_v2_20261026/internal_report.json) - under an hour. No GPU. Version B (core fine-tuning on confused pairs): one 12 GB GPU, the prepared script (300 steps x 8 episodes) plus FlyVis feature regeneration - hours, requires the author's approval and the 07:40 MSK weekday deadline rules.
